name: Flood-wyrm

baseline.name: Flood-wyrm
baseline.look: Long slate river animal with reedlike whiskers and four small paddle limbs.
baseline.ecology: Spawns in shallow reed beds; feeds on river mollusks.
baseline.limit: Responds to disturbance, not evil intent; upstream silt curls and stripped reeds warn of presence.
baseline.encounter: Give spawning grounds room and use high crossings; cannot burrow through stone.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: At first light an adult rakes mollusks out of river gravel with its whiskers. Its feeding grooves run with the current; a wagon dragged across the bed leaves a different mark. Adults withdraw into deeper bends when traffic grows.
cycle: Eggs adhere to submerged reed roots during the spring rise. Juveniles remain among stems while adults feed nearby. A spawning closure ends after local watchers record dispersal, never because a calendar page turns.
signs: A low silt curl travels upstream before the back breaks the surface. Newly stripped reeds and empty mollusk shells establish presence; ripples alone do not identify a wyrm.
escalation: Feeding -> head lift -> lateral body turn across a disturbed patch -> short defensive rush. Once intruders retreat, it protects the patch instead of pursuing them across dry country.
community: Reedbank watchers compare bank marks with boat crews. Closures hurt ferry income, so the kitchen buys from delayed fishers and the cooperative posts the next inspection time.
scene: A vanished wagon seems to have been taken by a wyrm. Hollis distinguishes feeding grooves from a mechanically pulled tow scar: the animal is real, but the accusation is wrong.
motion: Hold the long body silhouette; animate the whisker fan, gill beat and one continuous tail wave. A rush needs a planned path and splash hold, not a sequence of redesigned bodies.
sounds: Low water displacement, reed scrape, breathy surface exhalation. No speech, roar dialogue or mind link.
rule: Four small paddle limbs, long slate body, reedlike whiskers. Do not add horns, legs for running or stone-boring powers.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
